items.title: Stage Fort across Gloucester Harbor

vantage.basis: Lane's field drawing (inv. 109 + 222) and the catalogue viewpoint map
vantage.note: Stand on the Stage Fort Park side of the Blynman Bridge (the Cut), at the harbor edge, looking south. Stage Head and Tablet Rock fill the right half; Eastern Point light is the speck far left.

image.commons: Stage Fort across Gloucester Harbor MET DT5586.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Late-afternoon light on the overgrown 1620s settlement site. Lane's pencil study was ruled into eight equal panels — probably with a camera lucida — and the rocks in the painting register almost exactly with it.

items.title: Stage Rocks and Western Shore of Gloucester Outer Harbor

vantage.basis: Viewpoint chart for Lane's related drawing (inv. 107): end of Fort Point, or a boat just offshore
vantage.note: From the tip of Fort Point, look west-southwest across the outer harbor to the granite of Stage Head.

image.commons: Stage Rocks and Western Shore of Gloucester Outer Harbor, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1857, oil on canvas - National Gallery of Art, Washington - DSC00071.JPG

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Lane wrote to a friend that he'd sketched Stage Fort 'from the water' for a client who wanted it treated as a sunset. This canvas is in unusually pristine condition — close to how it looked coming off his easel.

items.title: The Old Fort and Ten Pound Island, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Catalogue commentary + proposed-viewpoint map (inv. 28/30): Duncan Street, on the fill that became Fear's Wharf
vantage.note: Bottom of Duncan Street at Harbor Loop — a block from Lane's own stone house — looking down Harbor Cove toward Ten Pound Island and Eastern Point.

image.commons: The Old Fort and Ten Pound Island, Gloucester, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1850s, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01162.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Harbor Cove as it looked in the early 1840s. A smaller unfinished version (inv. 28) shows Lane's method: he blocked in the landforms like a stage set, then populated it with vessels.

items.title: Ten Pound Island from Pavilion Beach

vantage.basis: Title + geography (Pavilion Beach faces Ten Pound Island across the harbor mouth)
vantage.note: Pavilion Beach, between the Fishermen's Memorial and Fort Point. Ten Pound Island light sits almost due south.

image.commons: Ten Pound Island from Pavilion Beach, by Fitz Henry Lane, . 1862, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01136.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Summer southwesterlies blow straight down the outer harbor onto Pavilion Beach; Lane shows vessels running fast for the inner harbor, about to drop sail amid hundreds of others.

items.title: Ten Pound Island, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Catalogue commentary: George Rogers's new wharf on Fort Point is the foreground
vantage.note: East side of Fort Point, by the wharves, looking south to the island.

image.commons: Ten Pound Island, Gloucester, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1850s, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01159.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Hazy late-summer light. The foreground is Rogers's wharf under construction — sharpened pilings stacked at the same angle as the lumber brig coming in.

items.title: Three Master on the Gloucester Railways

vantage.basis: Catalogue viewpoint chart (inv. 29): tip of Rocky Neck, 9° angle of view
vantage.note: North tip of Rocky Neck, looking across the inner harbor to Duncan's Point and Harbor Loop, where Maritime Gloucester keeps a working marine railway today. A very narrow view: zoom your camera in.

image.commons: Three Master on the Gloucester Railways, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1857, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01056.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Painted as a shop sign for John Trask's paint shop at the Burnham Brothers' marine railway. The ship California is hauled out for repairs; it later hung in City Hall.

items.title: Gloucester Harbor

vantage.basis: Catalogue viewpoint map (inv. 38): Babson's Ledge, off Fort Point
vantage.note: Lane worked from the water at Babson's Ledge. The closest dry land is the end of Pavilion Beach — look northeast at the city.

image.commons: Gloucester Harbor, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1852, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01203.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: A panorama commissioned by Sidney Mason, who built much of the new waterfront: the whole city of 1852, its wharves and church spires, under a huge still sky.

items.title: Gloucester Harbor

vantage.basis: Homer boarded at the corner of Main Street and Western Avenue in summer 1873
vantage.note: Exact spot not documented. This pin is Homer's 1873 lodging corner — the harbor he painted is a few steps south.

image.commons: Winslow Homer - Gloucester Harbor (1873).jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1910).
items.blurb: Homer's first Gloucester summer, when he also took up watercolor in earnest. He returned in 1880 and lived with the keeper on Ten Pound Island.

items.title: Gloucester Harbor from Rocky Neck

vantage.basis: Catalogue viewpoint chart (inv. 14)
vantage.note: West side of Rocky Neck, looking north-northwest across the inner harbor to downtown.

image.commons: Gloucester Harbor from Rocky Neck, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1844, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01134.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Painted two years before his 1846 lithograph from nearly the same spot — compare them side by side here.

items.title: View of Gloucester (From Rocky Neck)

vantage.basis: Catalogue: Rocky Neck, half the elevation and half the distance of the 1836 view; 82° angle of view
vantage.note: Same spot as the 1844 painting. Harbor Cove is compressed into the bottom third of the print.

image.commons: View of Gloucester from Rocky Neck, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1846, colored lithograph on paper by Lane and Scott's Lithography, Boston - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01119.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Lane's second Gloucester lithograph, sold to townspeople by Lane himself for a few dollars. Each of his three town views is larger and more detailed than the last.

items.title: View of Gloucester, Mass.

vantage.basis: Catalogue visual guide (inv. 446): about 50 ft south-west of the 1846 viewpoint, 74° angle of view
vantage.note: A few steps from the 1846 spot. The narrower view puts Fort Point and Duncan's Point front and centre.

image.commons: Fitz Henry Lane, View of Gloucester, Mass., 1855, NGA 145208.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: The largest and last of Lane's Gloucester prints (the NGA dates its impression 1855; the catalogue, 1859). Lane later mounted several on canvas, painted over them in oil, and sold them to friends for $25.

items.title: Ten Pound Island at Sunset

vantage.basis: Sunset glow behind the island ⇒ looking west from the Rocky Neck / East Gloucester shore
vantage.note: Wonson Street at Stevens Lane on Rocky Neck (Rocky Neck Art Trail stop 13); the public way runs down to the water.

image.commons: Ten Pound Island at Sunset, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1851, oil on panel - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01106.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Unusually moody for Lane: two men in a skiff reach for a mooring in deep twilight. The catalogue wonders whether his student Mary Blood Mellen had a hand in it.

items.title: View of the Town of Gloucester, Mass.

vantage.basis: Catalogue: twice the elevation and twice the distance from Harbor Cove of the 1846 Rocky Neck view; 92° view
vantage.note: Estimated: high ground in East Gloucester behind Rocky Neck. Walk the streets here and use the calibrate tool when the skyline lines up.

image.commons: Fitz Henry Lane (American, 1804-1865), Pendleton's Lithography (American, active 1825-1836) - View of the Town of Gloucester, Mass. - 2019.165 - Cleveland Museum of Art.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Lane's first view of his hometown, drawn on the stone himself at age 31. The high vantage gives an intimate look down on East Gloucester and a distant harbor village.

items.title: Gloucester Harbor

vantage.basis: Catalogue locator map (inv. 23): the shore at the head of the harbor — today largely filled
vantage.note: The 1847 shoreline here has been filled in; stand near East Main Street at the head of the inner harbor and look down-harbor past the State Fish Pier (once Five Pound Island).

image.commons: Gloucester Harbor, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1847, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01150.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Lane tries to fit his whole world into one view: wharves on both sides, Five Pound Island's fish shacks in the middle, Ten Pound light beyond, and a man caulking a boat on the beach.

items.title: The Church at Gloucester

vantage.basis: Subject: the Independent Christian (Universalist) Church, Middle & Church Streets, 1806
vantage.note: The church is certain; Hassam's exact spot isn't. Start on Middle Street south-east of the church and step around until the spire lines up.

image.commons: The Church at Gloucester MET DP161219.jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: Hassam painted this white Federal-style meetinghouse in 1918 and etched it the same year. Hopper painted the same steeple eight years later — all three are pinned here.

items.title: Colonial Church, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Same church as the Met painting
vantage.note: Same church, same year, as an etching.

image.commons: Childe Hassam, Colonial Church, Gloucester, 1918, NGA 32764.jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: Hassam's etching of the same meetinghouse.

items.title: Universalist Church

vantage.basis: Subject: the Universalist (Independent Christian) Church on Middle Street
vantage.note: Same steeple Hassam painted in 1918.

image.commons: Universalist Church (Edward Hopper, 1926).jpg

items.rights: Listed as public domain on Wikimedia Commons (US, 1926). Check the museum's terms before any public or commercial use.
items.blurb: Hopper first came to Gloucester in 1912 and returned in 1923, working in watercolor as Homer had fifty years before.

items.title: Gloucester, Mass. from Stage Fort Park

vantage.basis: Title; Stage Head is the high ground in the park facing the city
vantage.note: Top of Stage Head, looking north-east across the harbor to the city skyline.

image.commons: Gloucester, Mass. from Stage Fort Park, Gloucester, Mass (NYPL b12647398-75765).tiff

items.rights: Public domain (Detroit Publishing Co., pre-1929; NYPL Digital Collections).
items.blurb: Photographs are the easiest overlays to line up — a lens doesn't editorialise like a painter does.

items.title: Along Sea Wall, Stage Fort Park

vantage.basis: Title only
vantage.note: Somewhere along the harbor-side wall of Stage Fort Park.

image.commons: Along Sea Wall, Stage Fort Park, Gloucester, Mass (NYPL b12647398-75766).tiff

items.rights: Public domain (Detroit Publishing Co., pre-1929; NYPL Digital Collections).

items.title: Dolliver's Neck and the Western Shore from Field Beach

vantage.basis: Catalogue viewpoint drawing (inv. 3)
vantage.note: The beach just south-west of Stage Head (today's Cressy's Beach end of Stage Fort Park), looking down Fresh Water Cove to Dolliver's Neck.

image.commons: Dolliver's Neck and the Western Shore from Field Beach, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1857, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01201.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: One of the few pictures Lane described himself, in a letter to his patron Joseph Stevens: 'The effect is a mid day light with a cloudy sky, a patch of sunlight is thrown across the beach and the breaking waves…'

items.title: Fresh Water Cove from Dolliver's Neck, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Title + catalogue locator map
vantage.note: Dolliver's Neck is private residential. You can see the same cove from Hough Avenue and the Fresh Water Cove end of Western Avenue.

image.commons: Fitz Henry Lane - Fresh Water Cove from Dolliver's Neck, Gloucester - 48.445 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Fresh Water Cove had a spring, a road toward Salem and shelter behind Dolliver's Neck — reasons settlers came back here in the 1650s.

items.title: Brookbank, the Sawyer Homestead

vantage.basis: Subject: Samuel Sawyer's house at Fresh Water Cove, with the Fort and town behind
vantage.note: Around the head of Fresh Water Cove looking north-east; exact spot unknown.

image.commons: Samuel Sawyer Homestead, Freshwater Cover, Gloucester, by Fitz Henry Lane, c. 1860, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01168.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Sawyer — patron of Lane and of what became the Sawyer Free Library — before he added dormers to the house.

items.title: The Western Shore with Norman's Woe

vantage.basis: Catalogue viewpoint chart (inv. 18): head of Norman's Woe Cove
vantage.note: Shoreline here is private; the Hammond Castle grounds next door overlook the same rock.

image.commons: The Western Shore with Norman's Woe, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1862, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01220.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: A masterpiece of Lane's late luminism — calm cove, low tide, early twilight, and Longfellow's Norman's Woe glowing in the distance.

items.title: Babson and Ellery Houses, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Catalogue map showing Lane's viewpoint (inv. 10)
vantage.note: Both houses still stand on Washington Street. Lane's foreground salt marsh is now the Grant Circle rotary — view from the circle's edge, carefully.

image.commons: Babson and Ellery Houses by Fitz Henry Lane.png

alt.commons: Babson and Ellery Houses, Gloucester, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1863, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01213.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Commissioned by the Babson sisters before they moved west. The best place in town to see 'then and now' — the buildings are the same, the marsh is a traffic circle.

items.title: The Babson Meadows at Riverdale

vantage.basis: Catalogue: the view from behind the Babson homestead over Poplar Street and the Riverdale marshes
vantage.note: Behind the Babson house, looking out toward Poplar Street and the marsh.

image.commons: The Babson Meadows, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1863, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01217.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Companion to the Babson and Ellery Houses picture; a hay wagon nods to the family's haying business.

items.title: Looking up Squam River from 'Done Fudging'

vantage.basis: Catalogue commentary: the present-day Grant Circle rotary, looking west up the Annisquam
vantage.note: West edge of Grant Circle toward the Route 128 bridge.

image.commons: Looking Up 'Squam River from 'Done Fudging', by Fitz Henry Lane, c. 1850s, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01208.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: 'Fudging' was poling a river boat upstream against wind or tide — here you were done. Tiny canvas, enormous landscape.

items.title: Brace's Rock

vantage.basis: Title + geography: Brace Rock off the south-east shore of Brace Cove
vantage.note: The beach between Niles Pond and Brace Cove, looking south-east. Eastern Point Boulevard is a private way beyond its gate — check the signs before walking in.

image.commons: Brace's Rock, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1864, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01239.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: One of Lane's last subjects: a lone rock, a wreck, absolute stillness. He painted at least three versions, lowering the horizon each time to give the rock more presence.

items.title: Study of Brace's Rock, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Title
vantage.note: Same rock, thirty years after Lane.

image.commons: Frank Duveneck - Study of Braces Rock, Gloucester (c.1893).jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1919).
items.blurb: Duveneck summered in Gloucester for decades; his loose study makes a good foil to Lane's glassy version.

items.title: Eastern Point Light

vantage.basis: Subject; the lighthouse grounds are approached from the north-west
vantage.note: Lighthouse lot at the end of Eastern Point Blvd, near the start of the Dog Bar Breakwater.

image.commons: Eastern Point Light, Gloucester, Mass (NYPL b12647398-67903).tiff

items.rights: Public domain (Detroit Publishing Co., pre-1929; NYPL Digital Collections).
items.blurb: The 1890 brick tower at the harbor mouth; the Dog Bar Breakwater was being built around the time of this card.

items.title: Mother Ann

vantage.basis: Mother Ann is the rock profile on the shore just east of Eastern Point Light
vantage.note: Walk east of the lighthouse along the shore rocks.

image.commons: Mother Ann, Gloucester, Mass (NYPL b12647398-67902).tiff

items.rights: Public domain (Detroit Publishing Co., pre-1929; NYPL Digital Collections).
items.blurb: A granite outcrop by the lighthouse that locals have long seen as a woman's figure.

items.title: Good Harbor Beach, Bass Rocks

vantage.basis: Title; Bass Rocks is the headland at the beach's south end
vantage.note: From the Bass Rocks end, looking up the beach toward Salt Island.

image.commons: Good Harbor Beach, Bass Rocks, Gloucester, Mass (NYPL b12647398-75767).tiff

items.rights: Public domain (Detroit Publishing Co., pre-1929; NYPL Digital Collections).

items.title: Hawthorn Inn, E. Gloucester

vantage.basis: The Hawthorne Inn stood above Wonson Cove, off today's Hawthorne Lane
vantage.note: Compare the shoreline and hill from across Wonson Cove.

image.commons: Hawthorn Inn, E. Gloucester, Mass (NYPL b12647398-75764).tiff

items.rights: Public domain (Detroit Publishing Co., pre-1929; NYPL Digital Collections).
items.blurb: One of East Gloucester's summer hotels around 1900.

items.title: Annisquam Village

vantage.basis: Title only
vantage.note: Somewhere across Lobster Cove from the village; walk the footbridge and compare.

image.commons: Annisquam Village, Gloucester, Mass (NYPL b12647398-68949).tiff

items.rights: Public domain (Detroit Publishing Co., pre-1929; NYPL Digital Collections).

items.title: Lands End, Rockport, Mass.
items.medium: Lithograph, bird's-eye view (Meredith & Grew house-lot plan)
items.collection: Library of Congress, Geography & Map Division

vantage.basis: Aerial view — no single vantage on the ground
vantage.note: A bird's-eye view advertising house lots near the Turk's Head Inn. Thacher Island's twin lights lie just offshore.

image.commons: Lands End, Rockport, Mass. LOC 2007626395.jpg

items.rights: Public domain / no known restrictions (Library of Congress).
items.blurb: The kind of aerial town view that started all this — drawn from an imaginary point in the sky. Zoom in: the LOC scan is 11,751 px wide.

items.title: Squam Light

vantage.basis: Catherine Ryan's Hopper-in-Gloucester guide places it at 98 Wigwam Road, Annisquam; heading from the lighthouse position
vantage.note: Wigwam Road below Annisquam Light, looking up at the tower and keeper's house. The light station grounds are closed; the road is the way to see it.

image.commons: Squam Light, by Edward Hopper.webp

items.rights: Public domain in the US (made and published before 1931).
items.blurb: One of the handful of oils from Hopper's first Gloucester summer. He came back to the same light in 1923 for the watercolour Houses of 'Squam Light.

items.title: Prospect Street, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Ryan guide: houses at 98–102 Prospect Street, with the Our Lady of Good Voyage towers in the distance
vantage.note: Stand outside 98–102 Prospect Street and look east along the street. The twin blue domes of Our Lady of Good Voyage are your alignment mark.

image.commons: Prospect Street, Gloucester, by Edward Hopper.png

items.rights: Public domain in the US (made and published before 1931).
items.blurb: Hopper came back to this stretch of Prospect Street in 1934 for the oil Sun on Prospect Street. The church towers at the end of the road make this one of the easiest pictures in Gloucester to line up.

items.title: Railroad Gates

vantage.basis: Ryan guide: near the Gloucester commuter-rail stop, with St. Ann's spire (exaggerated by Hopper) as the landmark; heading toward St. Ann's, 74 Pleasant St
vantage.note: By the tracks near Gloucester station, looking toward St. Ann's church. Hopper stretched the spire, so match the rooflines rather than its height.

image.commons: Railroad Gates (1928) by Edward Hopper.jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (made and published before 1931).
items.blurb: Crossing gates, telegraph poles and a church spire — the railroad and the town pressed into one frame. Painted the same summer as Freight Cars, a few hundred feet away.

items.title: Freight Cars, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Ryan guide: Maplewood Avenue by the rail yard, St. Ann's spire as reference
vantage.note: Maplewood Avenue beside the tracks, looking southeast past the freight siding to the houses and St. Ann's spire.

image.commons: Freight Cars, Gloucester (1928) by Edward Hopper.jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (made and published before 1931).
items.blurb: A wall of boxcars cutting off the town behind it. The freight yard is mostly gone, but the houses and the spire survive.

items.title: Gloucester Roofs

vantage.basis: Ryan guide: 9 Winchester Court, reached by the public stairs from Main Street at Spring Street
vantage.note: Climb the Winchester Street stairs from Main at Spring; Hopper looked down over the roofs from the railing near 9 Winchester Court.

image.commons: Gloucester Roofs, by Edward Hopper.png

items.rights: Public domain in the US (made and published before 1931).
items.blurb: A view from a railing down onto a jumble of roofs — Hopper's favourite Gloucester subject was the houses, not the harbor.

items.title: Box Factory, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Ryan guide: Cleveland Street; the building with the span over the road has been razed
vantage.note: Cleveland Street, near the rail yard. The factory and its bridge are gone, so this is a then-and-now of an empty sky — match the street line.

image.commons: Box Factory, Gloucester, by Edward Hopper.png

items.rights: Public domain in the US (made and published before 1931).
items.blurb: A box factory's enclosed walkway bridging the street. Gone now, which makes it a good ghost.

items.title: Italian Quarter, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Ryan guide: The Fort, Commercial Street
vantage.note: The Fort neighbourhood off Commercial Street. Look for the green house against the granite.

image.commons: Italian Quarter, Gloucester, by Edward Hopper.jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (made and published before 1931).
items.blurb: Hopper's first Gloucester summer: a green house and its neighbours on the Fort, the old Italian fishing quarter.

items.title: Main Street, Gloucester
items.collection: New Britain Museum of American Art

vantage.basis: Title + the street's alignment; exact block not yet identified
vantage.note: Somewhere on Main Street near City Hall, looking along the old trolley line. Walk the street with the ghost up and stop where the building line and the far end match.

image.commons: Main Street, Gloucester, by John Sloan, 1917, oil on canvas - New Britain Museum of American Art - DSC09607.JPG

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: Shoppers, a trolley and a flag-hung street on a hot afternoon in 1917. A one-point perspective down the street — the easiest kind of picture to align in the ghost view.

items.title: Gloucester Towers

vantage.basis: City Hall's tower is the square tower; vantage on the hill north of it is a guess
vantage.note: From the hill above Main Street, line up City Hall's tower and the church spire beside it. Where they stand in the same relation as in the painting, you're in Sloan's spot.

image.commons: Gloucester Towers, by John Sloan.webp

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: Sloan spent five summers in East Gloucester (1914–18). Here the town is reduced to its towers against a heavy sky.

items.title: Gloucester Harbor

vantage.basis: Composition: high ground in East Gloucester looking across the inner harbor to downtown
vantage.note: From the slope above East Main Street, look west across the inner harbor. City Hall's tower should sit just right of centre.

image.commons: Childe Hassam - Gloucester Harbour (c. 1899).jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: Painted from the East Gloucester side: the whole inner harbor, the wharves and the city climbing behind.

items.title: Drydock, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Subject: a schooner hauled out on a marine railway — the Rocky Neck railway is the survivor
vantage.note: Gloucester Marine Railways at the tip of Rocky Neck, still hauling boats. The hull fills the frame, so this is about the scene, not a precise spot.

image.commons: Childe Hassam - Drydock, Gloucester - Google Art Project.jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: A schooner hauled out for painting, sails slack. The Rocky Neck railway has been doing this since 1859.

items.title: Gloucester Harbor

vantage.basis: Composition: hillside above the wharves looking across the harbor
vantage.note: East Gloucester hillside, looking down over the wharves to the harbor and the city.

image.commons: Willard Leroy Metcalf - Gloucester Harbour (1895).jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1925).
items.blurb: Metcalf's summer of 1895 in Gloucester: a bright hillside view down to the wharves.

items.title: Good Harbor Beach, Gloucester

vantage.basis: The footbridge over the creek to Good Harbor Beach (rebuilt 2018 on the same line)
vantage.note: Stand on the bank by the footbridge from the parking lot and look along it toward the beach.

image.commons: Leon Kroll - Good Harbor Beach, Gloucester (1912).jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: Bathers crossing the footbridge to Good Harbor Beach. The bridge has been rebuilt several times, always in the same place.

items.title: Half-Tide, Annisquam River

vantage.basis: Title; a low view across the river to the village houses
vantage.note: West bank of the Annisquam River, looking across to the village. Compare the shoreline at mid-tide.

image.commons: Beaux-half-tide-annisquam-river-1905.jpg

items.rights: Public domain in the US (published before 1931).
items.blurb: Beaux, best known for portraits, summered at Green Alley in Eastern Point. This is a pure landscape: the river at mid-tide and the houses beyond.

items.title: View of Coffin's Beach

vantage.basis: Lane's inscription: 'View of Coffin's beach, from the Rocks at the Loaf, after a sketch taken, August, 1862' (catalogue inv. 41)
vantage.note: The Loaf — the rocky outcrop at the Essex River end of Coffin's Beach. Look east along the beach; Annisquam and Lanesville are on the far shore.

image.commons: Fitz Henry Lane - View of Coffin's Beach - 53.383 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: Dawn over Ipswich Bay. Lane sketched it in August 1862 and inscribed exactly where he sat.

items.title: Gloucester from Brookbank

vantage.basis: Catalogue (inv. 42): the Brookbank series looks east from the Sawyer house over Fresh Water Cove to Dolliver's Neck and the harbor
vantage.note: Above Fresh Water Cove on the Sawyer homestead grounds, looking east over the cove to Dolliver's Neck and Ten Pound Island light.

image.commons: Fitz Henry Lane - Gloucester from Brookbank - 48.444 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: The first of Lane's views from Brookbank, the Sawyer family's farm. Same spot as the 1860 homestead picture, twelve years earlier.

items.title: Watch House Point

vantage.basis: Catalogue (inv. 292) names the point (the fort on Fort Point) but not Lane's vantage; this is a guess from the composition
vantage.note: From Rocky Neck, look west across the harbor to Fort Point — the old Watch House Point fort.

image.commons: Watch House Point, by Fitz Henry Lane, 1860, oil on canvas - Cape Ann Museum - Gloucester, MA - DSC01193.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: The fort on Watch House Point at sunset, small working boats in the foreground. Lane painted this point again and again.

items.title: View from Kettle Cove, Manchester-by-the-Sea

vantage.basis: Title only
vantage.note: Kettle Cove on the Manchester–Magnolia line. Look out to the islands offshore.

image.commons: Fitz Henry Lane - View from Kettle Cove, Manchester-by-the-Sea - 38.068 - Rhode Island School of Design Museum.jpg

items.rights: Public domain (artist died 1865).
items.blurb: An early, quiet Lane looking out from the Manchester shore.

items.title: The Fort and Ten Pound Island, Gloucester

vantage.basis: Same view as The Old Fort and Ten Pound Island (catalogue inv. 28/30): Duncan Street, looking down Harbor Cove
